items.title: terrainGrassGpu=off vs =on at ultra (and optionally high): standing and RUNNING, fresh profile per arm-rep, 3 reps, rotated order
items.boxMode: 1070, MODE T, fresh profile per arm-rep (each hbsess boot). OWNER-RUN.
items.reps: 3 per arm (2 minimum; the rule compares against the rep spread). Rotate the order each rep (suggestedOrder). High tier: the same with --quality high.
perArmRecipe: 2. node scripts/perf-worker/hbsess.mjs eval scripts/perf-worker/grass-gpu-run.eval.js > <OUT>/<arm>-r<rep>-run.json   (mode 'run': stand + run frame stats, long tasks, grass stats)

3. Running trace: write a one-line opts file  printf 'window.__grassGpuRunOpts={mode:"start"};return 1;' > <OUT>/gg-start-opts.js  and the same with mode "stop" > <OUT>/gg-stop-opts.js. Then: hbsess eval <OUT>/gg-start-opts.js; hbsess eval scripts/perf-worker/grass-gpu-run.eval.js (teleport, settle, AutoRun ON, returns); node scripts/perf-worker/gputrace.mjs <OUT>/<arm>-r<rep>-run.trace.json; python3 -I scripts/perf-worker/gpu_thread_split.py <OUT>/<arm>-r<rep>-run.trace.json; hbsess eval <OUT>/gg-stop-opts.js; hbsess eval scripts/perf-worker/grass-gpu-run.eval.js (AutoRun OFF + stats).

4. Running CPU profile: the same start / stop bracket around  node scripts/perf-worker/hbsess.mjs profile 10 <OUT>/<arm>-r<rep>-run.cpuprofile  → renderCPU and the grass update share (`node scripts/net-review/profile-split-render.mjs`; also search the profile for terrain_grass.js update / scatterInstance self time).
5. node scripts/perf-worker/hbsess.mjs kill; wait >= 65 s before the next boot.
reads: run.json: stand.{p50,p95,p99,longTasks} and run.{p50,p95,p99,max,longTasks,longTaskMs} (rAF intervals), runMetres, grassRun.instancesDrawn / tilesDrawn / levels[] (on) vs visibleBlades (off)
trace: CrGpuMain WEBGL ms/frame while running (the vertex-shader placement cost lands here), CrRendererMain busy
cpuprofile: renderCPU and the main-thread time in terrain_grass.js (off: the amortised re-scatter + instance uploads; on: the tile cull only)

off arm only, a hypothesis from the node bench (harness/bench_grass_cpu_vs_gpu.mjs): running east/west the CPU path re-uploads WHOLE instance buffers every frame (~6.7 MB/frame at ultra: an x-scroll touches more than maxUpdateRuns = 4 runs and falls back to a full upload). Look for large bufferSubData in the trace; it is a CPU-path issue independent of this flag.
decisionRules: Written 2026-10-23, BEFORE the run: flip ?terrainGrassGpu default ON (keeping `?terrainGrassGpu=off` as the escape) iff ALL of: (a) GG-BOOT is clean; (b) running main-thread frame time drops with `on` (run.p50 or renderCPU lower than `off` by more than the off arm's rep spread); (c) CrGpuMain WEBGL ms/frame while running does not rise by more than the rep spread; (d) GG-EYE is CLEAN.
If (b) holds but (c) fails: keep OFF; the vertex placement cost is too high on the 1070 — the next lever is the per-ring dead-blade share (stats levels[].instancesDrawn vs live) and the tile size.
If (b) fails: keep OFF; record the numbers. The node bench predicted 4.5–8.5x lower grass main-thread cost while running; a miss means the cost is elsewhere.
checklist: Every arm-rep: env shows the GTX 1070, frame cap 0, run.json errors [], start.landedOk true, start.tunnelStillActive false (else REJECT and re-run).
on arm: grassRun.mode === 'gpu'; off arm: grassRun.mode === 'cpu'.
Session end: test Chrome killed by user-data-dir.
out: RESULTS pointer + the rule verdict written back into this item's `result`.
